security_spec.violation_condition: When QEMU's MPT permission check reuses or delegates to the existing page-table walk machinery that consults mstatus.MXR, or when the MPT lookup path itself checks MXR, causing a load access to an MPT-protected execute-only (X=1,W=0,R=0) page to be incorrectly granted read permission because MXR makes the page appear readable.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: mstatus.MXR referenced or evaluated within the MPT access-type permission check path (step 7 of the MPT lookup algorithm); MPT XWR check that considers anything beyond the raw XWR bits; code paths where get_physical_address or similar TLB-fill functions consult MXR without first checking whether MPT is active
security_spec.summary: Spec explicitly forbids MXR and HLVX from overriding MPT permission bits; QEMU must check raw XWR bits in isolation without mstatus.MXR influence, else execute-only MPT pages become readable when MXR=1

findings.finding: QEMU does not implement the MPT (Memory Protection Table / Smmpt) extension at all. The get_physical_address function (lines 1537-1565) implements the standard Sv39/Sv48/Sv57 page-table walk with MXR handling for virtual-memory PTEs only. There is no MPT lookup path, no MPT entry format parsing, no mmpt CSR, and no MPT-specific permission check (step 7 of the MPT lookup algorithm). The spec violation — mstatus.MXR being consulted during MPT permission checks — cannot occur because the MPT infrastructure does not exist. However, this means any future MPT implementation that reuses or delegates to the existing get_physical_address code would inherit the MXR-vulnerable permission check and violate the PR #219 spec requirement that 'The MXR mechanisms or the use of HLVX instruction cannot be used to affect or override the interpretation of permissions encoded in memory-protection-table entries.'

spec_citations.excerpt: 7. Determine if the requested memory access is allowed by the XWR bits. If not, stop and raise an access-fault exception corresponding to the original access type, else the requested memory access is allowed. ** The MXR mechanisms or the use of HLVX instruction cannot be used to affect or override the interpretation of permissions encoded in memory-protection-table entries.
